newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Liberals behind in Atlantic.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Liberals behind in Atlantic.

text.p: Early voter returns in Canada's election on Monday showed a setback for Prime Minister Jean Chretien's Liberal Party in Atlantic Canada, with the Liberals losing at least seven seats and winning just two so far.

The Canadian Press news agency reported that the leftist New Democratic Party leader Alexa McDonough won her seat in Halifax, Nova Scotia, while Liberal Health Minister David Dingwall lost his seat in Nova Scotia to a New Democrat. Two other Liberal cabinet ministers including Defense Minister Doug Young, also trailed in their districts. The Liberals took 31 of 32 seats in Atlantic Canada in the 1993 election.
Liberal Fisheries Minister Fred Mifflin, who trounced his Conservative opponent by 75 percent to 21 percent in 1993, was battling to retain his seat in Newfoundland, Canadian Press said.

The results showed a sharp swing in support away from the Liberals, who dominated the region in the last election. The Conservatives were pulling ahead in some areas and the NDP in others, all at the Liberals' expense.
The preliminary Atlantic results were the first to trickle in after the polls in Newfoundland closed at 7 p.m. EDT and at 7:30 p.m. EDT in the other Atlantic provinces.
It was too early to forecast an outcome for the country as a whole, but the Atlantic provinces were a prime battleground for the Conservatives and the NDP against the Liberals.
